harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published node1’s approved release tree as the persistent, read-only rsync module `releases`. Node2 retrieved it to `/srv/rsync-releases-mirror` with file modes and symlinks intact. Write, sibling-module, and traversal attempts are denied. Both nodes were restarted individually and fully recovered without changing AlmaLinux 9.6 or kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.
actions_performed: Configured and enabled a hardened rsync daemon on node1, rooted at `/srv/legacy2/rsync-module-publication/releases`.
Enabled persistent SELinux read-only export access and restricted firewalld access to node2.
Retrieved the complete tree on node2 using archive semantics and verified hashes, modes, symlink target, and an empty itemized comparison.
Verified writes, access to the private sibling, and `../` traversal are rejected.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, proving changed boot identities and post-restart recovery.

evidence.requirement: Publish a read-only module named releases
evidence.summary: The enabled service is active; configuration names `releases`, uses the exact release-tree path, enables chroot and read-only mode, and live write attempts return `module is read only`.

evidence.requirement: Node2 retrieves the full tree with modes and symlinks intact
evidence.summary: Initial and post-restart retrievals show `current -> v1`, executable mode 755, matching hashes, and empty post-copy itemized comparisons.

evidence.requirement: Deny writes and access outside the module tree
evidence.summary: Uploads fail, the private sibling is an unknown module, and traversal remains confined to the releases root before and after restarts.
Source metadata and hashes remained unchanged; the private sibling remained present and no rejected write artifact appeared.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 and compatible rsync 3.2.5.
Boot ID changed from 31b01b46-96de-4ded-a021-49887e7d4053 to 6a85669d-8901-4a0a-840f-57c5dbc6b80d. The service, listener, source data, synchronization, and write denial recovered.
Boot ID changed from 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723 to db0e56e5-1d4c-469b-99a1-359e3a856c33. The mirror persisted and a fresh post-restart retrieval remained identical.
